rv.q: My over-riding feeling is that I've not seen a more richly achieved production at Trafalgar Studios since its conversion from the Whitehall in 2004.
Ned Bennett brilliantly directs the landmark 1973 play about a teenager who has blinded horses.
Posner's production wears these themes lightly, letting Shaffer's deft plotting and gently satirical humour shine out.
Bennett's production has an extraordinary visual language.
It is, ultimately, a superb revival, unflinching in its gaze, precise in its execution and deeply affecting in its impact.

cn.t: Critics praise this deeply impassioned revival of Shaffer's psychodrama for its striking intimacy and theatrical verve, with standout performances delivering a richly achieved production that honors the playwright's imaginative legacy.
